newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates slip as supply increases.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates slip as supply increases.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates slipped on Tuesday as arrival of fresh supplies increased and dealers said they expected the prices to ease further if exporters remained on the sidelines.
"The supply has exceeded demand which is dragging down the cotton prices," dealer Kishan Chand said. "Exporters are waiting for the prices to go down further towards the season's peak."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety from the 1996/97 crop was traded at 2,050 rupees ($61.73) per maund (37.32 kg) plus a 10 percent sales tax, while the MNH-93 was traded at 2,020, dealers said.
